posts.title: How we shipped a 16-section component library in one afternoon
posts.excerpt: Three principles for letting AI assemble production sites without DEMO-feel.
posts.contentHtml:
The trick wasn't the components — it was the manifest layer. By giving each section a JSON description with props, slot hints, and industry tags, the AI could pick the right one without us hardcoding flows.

Three principles

First: structure beats prompting. The agent doesn't invent a hero — it picks one of two pre-built variants. Second: separate visual decisions from content decisions. The theme tokens handle the first; the prompt handles the second. Third: every section gets a real Astro component with real props, not an HTML string.

posts.title: Industry theme tokens vs custom design tokens
posts.excerpt: When to lean on DaisyUI's variable system and when to roll your own.
posts.contentHtml: DaisyUI's --color-primary + --color-base-100 system covers ~80% of what you need. The remaining 20% is where bespoke token systems earn their keep.

posts.title: Static sites that feel alive (without JS)
posts.excerpt: Pure CSS interactions cover more ground than you think.
posts.contentHtml: Native <details> handles accordions. :checked + sibling selectors handle tabs. <dialog> handles modals via a checkbox toggle. The list goes on.
